prompts.title: Research workspace
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a high-fidelity desktop web application screen concept for the existing CivicSignal codebase.
Primary request: Create ONE complete, polished, plausible product screen, suitable for design review. CivicSignal joins Canadian statutes, bill metadata, short debate citations and news headlines through a metered API and MCP server, with a hosted BYOK research agent and embeddable widget planned. Its value is evidence and source provenance.
Style/medium: crisp, sophisticated flat UI screenshot, carefully typeset, editorial information hierarchy, very clear typography, strong alignment, abundant breathing room, refined thin borders, restrained neutral paper-like surfaces and charcoal text, one subdued accent used for active controls and selection. A quiet professional research tool with reading-friendly serif titles and a precise sans-serif UI, monospace only for code.
Composition/framing: one single desktop viewport in a landscape 16:10-ish composition, head-on, full bleed interface, all edges visible. No device, no perspective, no decorative backdrop, no photography, no collage, no giant marketing heading. Use a compact consistent application navigation rail, clear page toolbar and purposeful work area. Native sized text, readable fine detail.
Common identity and navigation, verbatim: "CivicSignal"; "Research"; "Briefs"; "Connect"; "Embed"; "Coverage". Use a small simple signal glyph, not a maple-leaf logo. Put a small "Design concept · Sample data" label in the footer.
Constraints: These are design proposals, not screenshots of implemented UI. Do not imply sample data is real live reporting. Every source item has an external-source affordance. News uses headlines and source metadata only; debate uses only short attributed excerpts or citation metadata; statutes may show text with an unofficial-version notice. Do not invent public-opinion polling. Do not invent long legal quotations or present made-up legal advice. Use the supplied short labels verbatim, concise exact typography, avoid filler text or lorem ipsum. No credit card imagery, stock art, gradients, glossy 3D, giant tiles, decorative flags, watermarks, or excessive pills. All mockups should feel part of one coherent product.
Screen: The hosted research-agent workspace envisaged in docs/HARNESS.md, with Research selected.
Layout: narrow navigation rail; a slim research-session list; generous central conversation and a useful source inspector occupying the right third. The output should feel like a working research session grounded in documents, not a generic chatbot.
Session list: "+ New research"; "Housing policy"; "Labour standards"; "Privacy and data". Current session title: "Housing policy".
Top toolbar: scope picker "Across Canada"; date filter "Last 7 days"; provider control "Your model · Connected".
User prompt, verbatim: "Which federal sources should I inspect on housing?"
Assistant heading: "Start with the evidence."
Concise answer, verbatim: "Review the legislation, then inspect bill status and debate citations. News headlines add context and link to the publisher." Render small inline citation markers [1] [2] [3].
Below this answer, show a compact evidence ledger with rows, not giant cards: "Legislation" / "National Housing Act" / "Official source"; "Bills" / "Housing-related bills" / "Status and identifiers"; "Debates" / "House of Commons" / "Citations and short excerpts"; "News" / "Publisher headlines" / "Headlines and links".
Show one unobtrusive completed retrieval activity line "Retrieved from 4 source types" with a check.
Right inspector titled "Source inspector": selected source "National Housing Act"; "Justice Laws Website"; compact fields "Type  Statute", "Jurisdiction  Federal", "Content  Full section text"; large action "Open official source ↗"; subtle note "Unofficial version. Check the official source." Below, a "Coverage" panel with "Federal records" available and "Municipal records" marked "Not covered".
Bottom composer: "Ask a follow-up about these sources…" and a send arrow; a compact row of command suggestions "/coverage" "/in-force" "/changes" marked as workspace commands. Keep everything readable and no long fake statutes.

Screen: A topic brief and geographic framing interface, with Briefs selected, titled "Housing".
Top line under title: "One topic. Every source in view." Controls: scope "Across Canada"; period "Last 7 days"; action "Refresh brief"; discreet "Sample brief".
The brief is the dominant content. Use a wide main evidence column and a narrower right context column, not a wall of equal metric tiles.
Across the evidence column, elegant restrained tab strip "All sources" selected; "Legislation 12"; "Bills 3"; "Debates 8"; "News 24". These are explicitly sample counts.
Evidence list with clearly different item anatomy:
1. "LEGISLATION" / "National Housing Act" / "Federal · Justice Laws Website" / label "In force" / action "Inspect source ↗". Two short metadata lines, no invented statute excerpt.
2. "BILL STATUS" / "Housing-related legislation" / "Parliament of Canada" / label "Status and identifiers" / action "Open bill record ↗". No invented bill number.
3. "DEBATE CITATION" / "Housing in the House of Commons" / "Hansard · Short attributed excerpts" / action "Open official debate ↗". Do not show a made-up speech or speaker.
4. "NEWS" / "City announces housing plan" / "Sample publisher · 2h ago" / "Headline and link only" / action "Read at publisher ↗". No article summary.
Right column: a geographic-distribution panel titled "Where this topic is active" with clean horizontal bars "Ontario 42%" "Quebec 24%" "British Columbia 18%" "Other 16%"; footnote "Sample distribution · 47 of 62 items geolocated". Under it a clear dropdown titled "Frame the question" with compact choices "Topic" selected, "Province", "Riding", "Municipality", "Region". Geography is a lens, not an on/off switch.
Below, a modest elegant line chart titled "Coverage tone" with a dotted zero baseline, a seven-day line, and note verbatim "Tone of news coverage, not public opinion." Attribution "GDELT".
Bottom visible row titled "Coverage" distinguish "Federal statutes · Available", "Provincial debates · Not covered", and "Gazette · No results" in sober text. Keep actual content readable, do not crowd.

Screen: A proposed embeddable widget configurator grounded in docs/PLAN.md wave 4, with Embed selected. Heading "Put the brief on your site". Subtitle "Choose a topic, frame the question, preview the result." Small label "Proposed interface".
Layout: a tidy configuration panel roughly 30 percent width and a much larger preview canvas. The preview canvas is a neutral inset area holding a real-looking clean compact CivicSignal widget, not an illustration or a generic website.
